title: 2007 AMC 10B Problem 17
statement: Point \(P\) is inside equilateral \(\triangle ABC.\) Points \(Q,\) \(R,\) and \(S\) are the feet of the perpendiculars from \(P\) to \(\overline{AB},\) \(\overline{BC},\) and \(\overline{CA},\) respectively. Given that \(PQ = 1,\) \(PR = 2,\) and \(PS = 3,\) what is \(AB?\)

solutions.text:
Let the side length be \(s.\) The perpendiculars from \(P\) are the heights of triangles \(APB,\) \(BPC,\) and \(CPA,\) so their areas are \(\dfrac{s}{2},\) \(s,\) and \(\dfrac{3s}{2}.\)

Their sum equals the area of \(\triangle ABC,\) which is also \(\dfrac{\sqrt3}{4}s^2.\) Hence \(3s=\dfrac{\sqrt3}{4}s^2.\)

The positive solution is \(s=4\sqrt3.\)

Thus, the correct answer is D.
hints: Connect \(P\) to the three vertices to split \(\triangle ABC\) into three smaller triangles
Their areas are \(\dfrac{s}{2},s,\dfrac{3s}{2}\); set the sum equal to \(\dfrac{\sqrt3}{4}s^2\)
